migrations: TypedBufferPool requires an explicit maxCachedBytes and returns immutable lease Handle; release takes that handle.
BufferProvider.withBuffer is async throws with Sendable body/result; release is awaited on both exits.

Actor handles are borrowed metadata: retain provider through release, initialize/deinitialize used generic elements, and synchronize pointer access independently. MemoryPool handles retain allocation owners and may outlive their pool.
limitations: No real OOM recovery claim; per-instance deterministic allocation failures exercise fallback routes.
Cancellation retains the lease until the scoped body completes, including a body that ignores cancellation.
